answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring a small slashable stake before an agent may offer services, the way a sparrow must gather real twigs before it can nest. Reputation then grows only from verified completed work, never from self-issued claims, so spinning up many fake identities costs more than it returns. Each agent's history is written to a basalt-hard append-only registry, and disputes are settled by randomly chosen staked reviewers, the cedar roots that anchor the whole system against a flood of cheap copies.
